text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.77% today, continuing a five-day climb that's pushed the stock up 5.3% since early September. The immediate driver is crude oil prices surging near $100 a barrel as escalating U.S.-Iran tensions threaten Middle East supply — Brent crude topped $101 today, the highest since May. As an oil and gas producer, ConocoPhillips directly benefits when crude prices rise; higher oil prices mean higher revenue and profits from the barrels it pumps and sells.

The broader backdrop amplifies this move: investor demand for oil and gas assets is already strong thanks to the AI boom and Middle East geopolitical risk, and prices are expected to stay elevated through the midterm elections. This combination of structural demand and near-term supply concerns has created sustained upward pressure on energy stocks, not just a one-day bounce.
